title: Sally adds Buy now with Stripe

voice.instructions: Warm, confident and unhurried, like a founder telling a customer's story. Plain American English. Slight smile in the voice. Pause briefly at each sentence end.

scenes.text: Meet Sally. She sells home and hardware products online, and she has grown her site one step at a time with the Accelerator from Strategic Machines. She doesn't write code. She knows how to sell.

Today's step: let shoppers pick a product, pay with Stripe, and have it shipped. Sally just says so. Her Team Lead rates it High, because money moves, and tells her exactly where she will be asked to decide.
The Designer writes it up in plain English: a Buy now button, Stripe Checkout, the price always from the catalog, flat-rate shipping, and test mode only. Sally reads it, and approves.
She sets the mandate: what's in scope, what must never break, and a budget. The Planner breaks the work into four small steps, each with its own tests. Approved.
Now the crew works. Every step adds its own tests, and nothing moves on until all of them pass. Two hundred forty-three tests became two hundred seventy-six.
The Judge proves the exact candidate and opens a preview. Sally buys a cordless drill with Stripe's test card, and the order lands in Stripe. She approves the release.
It's live. And every decision, every test run and every handoff is on the record: on Sally's timeline, and in her own repository.
Sally sells. The crew builds. And nothing ships without her say-so. The Accelerator, from Strategic Machines.
